title: Machine-produced evidence ledger entry (one command execution)
description: Normative contract for one entry of the hash-chained evidence ledger (document 06 section 3.1, constitution 11.4.115(H), 11.4.245, 11.4.268). Changes against the document 06 draft: (1) `redacted` added, because rule 8 of document 06 writes `redacted: true` while the draft sets additionalProperties false; (2) conditional rules 1, 4, 5 and the blocked-reason pairing are expressed in the schema instead of prose; (3) `blocked_reason` requires verdict `blocked`. Producer: the evidence recorder (document 06 section 13 POC `evrec.sh`, production tool to be built test-first). Consumers: verdict deriver (verdict/1), register importer (reg_evidence rows), report checker for FR-022 and SC-012. No real ledger exists yet, so this schema was validated only against synthetic golden-good and golden-bad fixtures (see contracts/README.md). Revision 2 (independent review 2026-10-03): verdict is tied to exit status by rule 10 of document 06 section 3.1 (pass <=> exit 0; fail <=> exit 1..125, the test ran and its assertion failed; error <=> 126, 127, 128+ or negative, i.e. not executable, not found or killed by a signal, no test outcome); a RED entry must not be `pass`, a GREEN entry must be `pass`, a caught mutation must be `fail`; `target_class` and `target_ref` added so the verdict deriver can require that RED and GREEN ran the same test (same argv, cwd, target class and target locator) on different fingerprints; `item` accepts only canonical ids (the finding alias F-<unit>-NNN is not an evidence key). Revision 3 (second independent review 2026-10-03): `test_fingerprint` (sha256 of the resolved argv[0] file plus declared test sources, taken before the run) is required on RED, GREEN and MUTATION entries whose verdict is `pass` or `fail`, so the deriver can refuse a RED produced by different test bytes than the GREEN (rule 11); a `MUTATION` entry requires its `mutation` object (rule 12); `blocked_detail` (human-readable observed values, credential variable names only) and `counts_as` (`not_passing`) are added and required with `verdict: blocked`, matching document 05 section 10. Ordering (every RED before every GREEN) and the three distinct GREEN iterations are cross-entry rules checked by the verdict deriver, not by this per-entry schema. Revision 4 (third independent review 2026-10-03): polarity `REOPEN` added: the entry that records the observed recurrence of a closed item; it requires `verdict`, `target_class` and `target_ref`, and the verdict deriver evaluates only the item's entries recorded after its last `REOPEN` entry (document 06 section 4.2 step 7, cycle rule). Revision 5 (fourth independent review 2026-10-03): a `REOPEN` entry must be a genuine test failure, `verdict: fail` with `exit_status` 1..125 (a passing run, a harness error or a blocked probe observed no recurrence and is not a `REOPEN`); the deriver additionally counts a `REOPEN` as a cycle cut only when it is the same test as the cycle it ends and that cycle derived PASS, and refuses a GREEN on a fingerprint that a cutting `REOPEN` showed failing or that was GREEN in an earlier cycle (document 06 section 4.2 step 7). `exit_status` of a `blocked` entry is defined: the test command was not run, and `exit_status` is the exit status of the failing precondition probe, which must be non-zero (a probe that exited 0 cannot block); the same closed `blocked_reason` set is the CHECK on `reg_test_runs.blocked_reason` (document 04). Revision 6 (contracts revision 19, analyze-remediation finding A10, 2026-10-05; additive): optional `pre_release` (boolean) and `test_state_gos` (non-empty array of unique strings) added for the pre-release production form of tasks.md T042 CENTRAL C8 (ii); `pre_release: true` requires `test_state_gos`, and `test_state_gos` requires `pre_release: true`; no existing keyword changed, so every entry that carries neither new property gets the same result under revision 5 and revision 6 (valid stays valid, refused stays refused; only entries carrying the new properties, all refused by revision 5's additionalProperties false, can change), and the `$id` stays `ev/1`. tasks.md T042 CENTRAL C8 (ii) and T048a name the field `test_state_gos`; the name stays UNCONFIRMED until T048a lands (amended after the independent review of 2026-10-05, finding A-4; description only). Revision 7 (contracts revision 20, owner decision ODG-11 of 2026-10-05; NOT backward compatible for the old prefix): the register-id alternative of the `item` pattern is `CAT-[0-9]{3,}` instead of the withdrawn prefix's pattern; every other keyword is unchanged (`additionalProperties` rules kept), so an `item` carrying the withdrawn prefix, valid under revision 6, is refused under revision 7 and CAT-001 is valid; the `$id` stays `ev/1` because no ledger exists yet.

item.description: exact stable id of the register item, finding or run the entry belongs to

argv.description: genuine argument list, never a shell-joined string

exit_status.description: exit status of the test command; for `verdict: blocked` the command was not run and this is the exit status of the failing precondition probe (non-zero)

target_class.description: document 06 section 6 target class; RED and GREEN of one closure must share it

target_ref.description: stable locator of the fingerprinted target (path, image name, package name plus device serial); RED and GREEN of one closure must share it while their fingerprints differ

test_fingerprint.description: sha256 of the file argv[0] resolves to combined with the sha256 of every declared test source, taken before the command runs (document 06 section 3.1 rule 11); RED and GREEN of one closure must share it. When argv[0] is an interpreter the test sources must be declared, otherwise this hashes only the interpreter

prev_hash.description: entry_hash of seq-1; 64 zeros for seq 1

entry_hash.description: sha256 of the canonical JSON of this entry without entry_hash

verdict.description: outcome of the command, derived from exit_status by the recorder (document 06 section 3.1 rule 10); `blocked` is set by the harness when a precondition probe failed

blocked_detail.description: human-readable observed values behind the blocked_reason (document 05 section 10); credential variable names only, never values (11.4.10)

counts_as.description: a blocked entry is never a pass or a skip; it counts as not passing for SC-004 and completion (document 05 section 10)

closes_item.description: true when this entry is part of the RED/GREEN pair that closes a register item

redacted.description: true when a credential value was found in argv or a stream and replaced before writing (11.4.10)

pre_release.description: Revision 6 (contracts revision 19). true marks the entry of a run made in the pre-release production form of tasks.md T042 CENTRAL C8 (ii): the script ran on the T039 harness through the test-state `cpa-host --exec-approved`, never through the owner's state; its output file carries a top-level `"pre_release": true`. With true, `test_state_gos` is required. The consumers T564a, T569, T580, T580a and T582 refuse such an entry and the output it cites with 20 `pre_release_output`; that refusal is theirs, not this schema's. Optional: entries written before revision 6 carry no `pre_release` and stay valid.

test_state_gos.description: Revision 6 (contracts revision 19). The GOs that the test state approved for a `pre_release` run (tasks.md T042 CENTRAL C8 (ii): every committed GO the run needs that the owner had not approved, in the order of their introductions, then LAST the fixture `G-GATE` GO of the CENTRAL C3 (a) form), one string per GO naming its verdict file. Allowed only with `pre_release: true`. tasks.md T042 CENTRAL C8 (ii) and T048a name the field `test_state_gos` (each such GO 'named in the run's `ev/1` entry'); the name and the one-string-per-verdict-file form, chosen by the contracts revision 19 author, stay UNCONFIRMED until T048a lands.
